page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at up to 3.9 GHz, it provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance includes 480 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for advanced vector and matrix operations, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (tile and int8). Memory capacity is 96 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, delivering a compute-centric 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle discrete GPUs or local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote EBS volumes for persistent data. Baseline networking throughput is rated at 11 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory performance. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,330.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 69,241.15. Cache and memory subsystems yielded 193.31 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations, facilitating high-throughput operations such as static web serving (82.41 GB/sec) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (336.47 GB/sec). Hardware-accelerated matrix instructions provide high-throughput AI execution, recording 348.34 tokens per second in 135M parameter LLM text generation and 29.72 tokens per second on 7B models. PassMark database tests recorded 22,992.82 points, with Redis operations achieving 86.83 million SET operations per second.

As part of the flex series with a burstable CPU allocation profile, the instance offers a cost-effective alternative to fixed compute configurations. It maximizes resource density for variable workloads, trading dedicated continuous peak CPU allocation for lower compute expenses. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires external network storage planning, but the balance of 48 high-clock vCPUs, DDR5 memory bandwidth, and AMX acceleration makes it an efficient platform for batch processing, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
